answer.rationale: Write-path latency began climbing 90 minutes ago, shortly after a release 2 hours prior, making a bad build the most plausible proximate cause. memory_b1 shows rollback safely cleared a similar checkout error spike with no customer impact, supporting this as the lowest-risk intervention. Regional failover (memory_b2) is explicitly contraindicated right now because writes are hot and settlement traffic is at peak—failover previously caused a 40-minute replication gap and lost writes under identical conditions, which directly conflicts with the objective of not losing customer writes. Add_capacity or read-replica routing don't address a release-correlated regression, and circuit breakers would shed load rather than fix root cause. I verified b1 and b2 specifically because they represent the leading candidate action and the most dangerous rejected alternative, so confirming their original details before committing capacity is highest-value. Proceeding with a standard (not maximal) rollout of the rollback to allow quick confirmation that latency responds before fully committing, given some uncertainty remains about whether capacity strain is compounding the release issue.
